decision: Reclassified as an electrical emergency (burning smell + warm socket face persisting ~8.5 hours, child in occupation). Sent the rulebook electrical first action to the tenant (ACT-1), instructed an emergency electrician for make-safe attendance up to £250 under CAP-DISPATCH-EMERGENCY (ACT-2, overriding the landlord's "handyman only / keep costs controlled" instruction at event-006/event-016), informed the landlord of the hazard, dispatch and cost band (ACT-3), logged the file note (ACT-4). Escalating to the property manager for welfare follow-up (ESC-VULNERABLE), confirmation of attendance, and the repair-spend decision above the £250 make-safe ceiling (APR-EMERGENCY-REPAIR) — the landlord has not replied to the authority requests at event-020 and event-024.
recap: Kitchen socket burning smell reclassified as an electrical emergency: tenant given safety advice, emergency electrician instructed to make safe, landlord told, handed to manager.
next_step: Property manager to make a welfare call to the tenant this evening, confirm the electrician's attendance/ETA, and obtain landlord or on-call manager approval for any remedial repair above the £250 make-safe ceiling.

facts.statement: Tenant reported a hot/burning smell at the kitchen counter socket and a warm socket face at 08:14 on 2025-04-12 after a kettle was used; kettle unplugged.
At 16:42 the faint burning smell was still noticeable, the socket unused, no breaker switched off and the fridge still powered.
Occupant household includes a 10-year-old child; tenant was alone with him at the property during the day.
No emergency-response guidance had been communicated to the tenant before this agent's message.
The landlord's handyman Rowan Pike does not carry out fixed-wiring repairs and has no electrical test equipment; he did not enter the property and no inspection or isolation took place.
Landlord asked for costs to be controlled, nominated his handyman, and has not approved an electrician call-out or any electrical repair; he did not answer the authority requests at 13:14 and 15:02.
Tenant consented to a contractor visit and to sharing symptoms and access details on 2025-04-12 (event-013); she is back at the property from about 16:30.

# Kitchen socket maintenance request

## Case details
- source role: Tenant
- created: 2025-04-12 08:14:00 UTC
- property: 8 Brindlewick Row, Oakhollow, ZZ1 1ZZ

## Initial request
There is a hot smell near the kitchen socket by the counter, and the socket face feels warm. Please arrange an inspection. I am not sure whether the socket is safe to use.

input.message: Nora — treating this as an electrical emergency. Please do the following now: (1) Do not use or touch the kitchen socket, and leave the kettle unplugged. (2) If it is safe to reach the consumer unit, switch off the breaker serving the kitchen sockets; if you cannot identify it, switch off the main switch — the fridge may lose power, which is acceptable for a short period. Do not open the consumer unit or remove any cover. (3) If you see smoke or sparks, or the burning smell gets stronger, leave the property with your son and call 999. (4) Keep a window open in the kitchen. An emergency electrician is being instructed now to attend today to inspect, test and make safe; they will contact you to confirm a time. Please reply to confirm you can give access this evening. We will stay with this until it is made safe.

input.description: EMERGENCY make-safe at 8 Brindlewick Row, Oakhollow, ZZ1 1ZZ. Tenant reports a hot/burning smell at the kitchen counter socket and a warm socket face, reported 08:14 and still present at 16:42 (event-001, event-017, event-025). No smoke or sparks seen; kettle unplugged; circuit not isolated; no inspection has taken place (event-023). Attend today: identify and isolate the affected circuit, inspect/test the socket and connections, make safe (isolate or replace accessory as needed) and report findings. Make-safe attendance only under the agency's emergency authority (max £250); any further repair must be quoted and approved before it is carried out. Occupant present from 16:30, priority attendance, household includes a child — contact tenant to confirm access window.

gate.reason: Safety duty overrides the landlord's cap for MAKING SAFE (s.11 Landlord and Tenant Act 1985, gas and electrical safety regulations): attendance, isolation, temporary heaters, boarding, a locksmith, up to £250 without anyone's approval. The repair itself above that is not covered: it goes to the landlord or the on-call manager now, with the quote and the deadline (APR-EMERGENCY-REPAIR). Notify the landlord immediately after dispatch.
